en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, which is significantly more than the previously recorded 7,107.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level in Davao.
Taal Volcano is the second most active volcano in the Philippines, having erupted 38 times in recorded history.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Philippine Trench is the deepest part of the Philippine seas, plunging to a maximum depth of 10,540 meters.
The Puerto Princesa underground river stretches for 8.2 kilometers, making it one of the longest navigable subterranean rivers worldwide.
The Banaue Rice Terraces stretch for about 1,036 kilometers, which would encircle half the globe if placed end-to-end.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 97,030 hectares of pristine marine habitat in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
Cebu is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching about 225 kilometers from its northern to southern tips.
Mount Mayon in Albay is the most active volcano in the Philippines, having erupted over 50 times since 1616.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering roughly 14,649 square kilometers of territory.
